analysis:
Examined all supplied CI source, changed ranges, and docs-impact metadata/patch. CI now restores .git before checkout, saves it only on master/dev pushes, disables checkout credential persistence, and retries cold after checkout failure (.github/workflows/ci.yml:17–25, 60–101 and repeated checkout sequences). Full-history Docs Lint uses a separate cache family (179–211). Sparse checkout excludes evidence archives/videos elsewhere; docs-impact retains full commit history while adding partial-clone and sparse settings (.github/workflows/docs-impact.yml:61–68). No concrete credential disclosure, PR-to-trusted-branch cache poisoning, or weakened runtime authorization/encryption control is established by these changes. Provider/cache/media gates remain visible; test selection and final gate behavior are not changed here (ci.yml:1230–1262). T-041 runtime cache isolation and A-001/A-003 protections are not altered by the CI caches.
Integration should reconcile the new SAVE_CACHES inputs with .github/actions/provider-ci-build (ci.yml:284–287, 532–535, 735–738, 1087–1090), and verify cache producer/consumer trust separation for the routed Linux jobs (41–54, 164–167), including whether their runner environments are trusted to produce reusable .git state. The supplied scope does not establish that contract or any release workflow consumption of these cache families; neither is evidence of a vulnerability. Also verify the changed cluster build identity remains sufficient when refs from cached .git differ (952–980). These contracts matter to build-integrity assumptions associated with A-011/A-017 and T-054. No direct change to billing, attestation proof validation, fan authority, or sandbox installer execution is visible. Missing referenced implementations limit this source pass rather than establish safety.
